column1: # The per-tool guides for proxy mode (W8, part 3b; ADR 0041, "How the per-tool guides are built"; docs/VPN.md, "Proxy
# mode, step by step"). One row per guide, in the order of the tool usage matrix (global, read 2026-11-21) among the
# tools with a proxy mode, then the rest of tools.tsv's proxy tools in its order, then the tools that run only as a VPN.
# Steps and notes are in guide-steps.tsv, the tools' own labels in guide-labels.tsv. scripts/guides.py checks all three
# against tools.tsv, and writes the website's pages from them and Watch's English strings.
#   guide            the guide's name, also its page's: docs/site/guides/<guide>/
#   packages         the tools.tsv packages it covers, comma separated
#   page             proxy (steps to run the tool in its proxy mode), wireguard (it runs only as a VPN, and Watch carries a
#                    WireGuard configuration instead, W7), vpn (it runs only as a VPN: Watch cannot run beside it), or
#                    waiting (no steps until a check on a phone)
#   version          the tool's version the steps are read at; '-' for none
#   source           the repository at that version's release tag
#   commit           the commit the tag points to; every link of this guide's steps and labels is at it
#   listener         the SOCKS5 and HTTP listeners in proxy mode, as tools.tsv's proxy column; where tools.tsv says 'profile',
#                    the one the guide's steps set, which Watch's finder greets
#   listener-source  the line that sets that default, or names the field
#   auth-source      the line that shows it
#   checked          the version tried with Watch on a phone (docs/spikes/2026-11-real-tools.md), or waiting: a tool waits for
#                    a device check until the maintainer gives the word for it (the 2026-11-11 method: the developer's own
